name: Two Truths and a Myth
why_it_works: People love proving they know better, and a three-way pick is easy enough to answer without thinking. When the myth turns out to be the one they believed, the professional who corrected them gains instant credibility without ever sounding like an ad.

hook.pattern: Promise three statements, one false, and say the false one costs people.
examples: Two of these are true. One costs people thousands. Which?
Most people pick the wrong one. Let's see if you do.
Three {{topic}} facts. One is a myth. Comment your number.

variables.name: truth_one
variables.example: Brushing right after coffee can wear enamel

variables.name: truth_two
variables.example: Gums can bleed with no pain at all

variables.name: myth
variables.description: The common belief that is false
variables.example: If it doesn't hurt, there's no cavity

variables.name: myth_fix
variables.description: One plain sentence on what's actually true
variables.example: Most early cavities don't hurt; that's why checkups find them

beats.purpose: hook: one of three is false
beats.voiceover: Two of these are true. One is a myth that costs people.

craft.notes: Put the myth in the middle slot and phrase it in the exact words people use, so it sounds the most familiar. Rotate the myth's position in future posts so regular viewers can't game it.

do_not: Use a myth so obvious nobody believed it; the payoff needs the 'wait, really?' moment
Shame people who got it wrong in replies
Answer individual cases in the comments; move them to a private consult
compliance: Law firms: no promises or predictions of case outcomes; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires it; general information, not legal advice
Dental, chiropractic: no cure or guaranteed-result claims; treatment statements must be supported and say results vary
Financial advisors: no return or income promises; say it is educational, not personalized advice; follow your firm's compliance review before posting
Insurance: never imply a claim will be approved or a policy covers something without checking the policy terms; include license number where required
